definitions.explanation: Replacing existing data or content by writing new data in its place. Most commonly used in computing contexts.

definitions.gloss: address written on the outside of a letter
definitions.explanation: The name and address written on the outside of an envelope or package. A traditional usage.

examples.japanese: ファイルを{上書|うわが}き{保存|ほぞん}する。
examples.english: To save a file by overwriting it.

examples.japanese: {間違|まちが}えて{上書|うわが}きしてしまった。
{大事|だいじ}なデータを{上書|うわが}きしないように{気|き}をつけてください。
examples.english: Please be careful not to overwrite important data.

examples.japanese: {封筒|ふうとう}の{上書|うわが}きを{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: To check the address on the envelope.

notes:
{上書|うわが}き has two meanings: overwriting data (computing) and the address on an envelope (traditional). The computing sense is far more common today.

COMPUTING USAGE:
- {上書|うわが}き{保存|ほぞん}: Save (overwrite existing file) — equivalent to Ctrl+S
- {名前|なまえ}をつけて{保存|ほぞん}: Save As — saves as a new file
- {上書|うわが}き{禁止|きんし}: write-protected, overwrite not allowed

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {上書|うわが}きする: to overwrite
- {上書|うわが}きされる: to be overwritten
- {間違|まちが}えて{上書|うわが}きする: to accidentally overwrite

TRADITIONAL USAGE:
In letter-writing, {上書|うわが}き refers to the name and address written on the outside of an envelope ({封筒|ふうとう}). This usage is now less common but still appears in formal contexts.

ETYMOLOGY:
From {上|うえ} (on top) + {書|か}き (writing) — writing on top of something.
